methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses integrated molecular profiling (scRNA-seq datasets with adjacent dura, joint single-nucleus RNA-seq/ATAC-seq multiome on meningiomas, and spatial multiplex immunofluorescence) to identify dominant immunosuppressive features and STING targetability within the meningioma microenvironment (Results: immune landscape and collagen/LAIR-1 findings; Methods: multiome profiling and analysis). It combines these observational analyses with functional perturbations in patient-derived ex vivo tissue (8803 treatment inducing cytotoxicity and inflammatory cell death features such as gasdermin D pore formation) and with in vivo efficacy, including randomized preclinical survival studies with stated power calculations (Methods: Statistical analysis; Figures 7–9 descriptions in Discussion/Figures). Mechanistic steps are supported by orthogonal assays spanning macrophage exposure to mechanically lysed tumor material with genotype controls (WT vs MyD88-/- vs STING-deficient macrophages) and multiplex cytokine/chemokine readouts, which helps separate direct drug effects from DAMP-driven effects (Results: macrophage activation; Methods: macrophage and Luminex assays). Statistical reporting includes ANOVA-based pairwise comparisons, linear regression interaction modeling for Luminex, and log-rank/Cox-based survival design considerations; however, many analyses are multi-endpoint and the normalized text does not consistently specify multiplicity control beyond FDR in single-cell neighborhood/DE testing (Methods: Statistical analysis; Results figure legends).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The manuscript targets a clinically unmet need in meningiomas (limited systemic therapies beyond surgery/radiation) and proposes a STING agonist (8803) as a local therapeutic strategy that can both kill tumor cells ex vivo and remodel the immune microenvironment in vivo (Abstract; Discussion). On the Oxford CEBM scale, the evidence is preclinical and ex vivo (patient tissue treated outside the body plus mouse models), without patient intervention/outcome data, so it maps to LoE 5 (Methods/Results). Translational relevance is supported by use of freshly resected patient meningioma samples for ex vivo response assessment and by demonstration of survival benefit in orthotopic models, including an immunocompetent setting with immune infiltration changes (Abstract; Discussion/Fig. 8 description). The key limitation for immediate clinical inference is that dosing, delivery, safety, and efficacy are not tested in a human trial, and the clinical endpoints are inferred from preclinical survival and microenvironment changes (Discussion).

reporting_quality.justification: Given the prominence of animal efficacy and survival studies (flank and orthotopic models, including immunocompetent experiments) ARRIVE is the most applicable reporting standard, and the Methods include IACUC/IRB approvals, humane endpoints, tumor-measurement formulas, and explicit randomization statements (Methods: Ethics statement; Methods: Statistical analysis). The manuscript reports key sample sizes for major analyses (e.g., scRNA-seq immune-cell counts and patient numbers, n = 4 multiome meningiomas, and n values for orthotopic survival arms and Luminex replicates) and uses appropriate statistical frameworks for high-dimensional data (FDR-corrected negative binomial GLM for neighborhood DA; Wilcoxon tests for DE; regression interaction modeling for Luminex) (Results Fig. 1–2 legend; Methods; Figures 8–9 descriptions). Some details relevant to reproducibility are referenced to prior datasets/tables and the Nature reporting summary, and the normalized text does not provide explicit repository links for raw sequencing data or analysis code, so transparency is moderate (Methods: references to public repositories; Reporting summary note). Overall, the reporting is strong for study design and core methods, with minor gaps mainly in explicit data/code deposition statements in this version (Methods/Additional Sections).

novelty_literature.justification: A novel element is the demonstration that STING activation is broadly targetable in both neoplastic and immune compartments of meningiomas and can induce direct tumor cytotoxicity via inflammatory cell death pathways (including GSDMD pore formation) rather than purely immune-mediated effects (Abstract; Discussion). The work also links STING-agonist-induced tumor lysis to macrophage activation and extracellular matrix remodeling (e.g., induction of MMP-3 and depletion of collagen such as COL6A in treated tumors), connecting immunogenic cell death to a meningioma-specific stromal feature (Results: macrophage activation and COL6A findings; Figures 9E–F description). While STING agonists have been studied in other solid tumors, positioning meningiomas as a setting with robust STING locus accessibility/expression and a collagen/LAIR-1 immunosuppressive niche provides a distinctive mechanistic and translational framing (Abstract; Results; Discussion). The contribution is preclinical rather than clinical-first-in-human, so novelty is strong but not yet practice-changing (Discussion).

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript follows a clear structure from immune landscape characterization (collagen/LAIR-1 and TAM enrichment) to therapeutic targeting rationale and then to functional validation in ex vivo patient material and orthotopic in vivo models (Results; Discussion). Methods are detailed for major platforms (10x multiome processing, Seurat/Harmony/WNN integration steps, macrophage preparation, Luminex workflow, and survival-study considerations), supporting reader comprehension and replication (Methods). Figure legends (as preserved) are information-dense and include analysis choices and sample sizes, which helps interpret the work without access to figure images in this normalized corpus (Results/Figures excerpts). Some technical sections are dense due to multi-omics tooling, but the main narrative claims remain traceable to specific assays and reported n values (Methods/Results).

key_strengths: Multi-modal profiling (scRNA-seq with dura comparators, multiome RNA+ATAC, and spatial multiplex IF) identifies collagen/LAIR-1-associated immunosuppression and STING expression/accessibility as actionable features in meningiomas (Results; Methods).

Functional evidence shows 8803 induces direct tumor cytotoxicity and inflammatory cell death signaling, and links tumor lysis to macrophage activation and cytokine/MMP induction using genotype-controlled macrophages (Results; Methods: MyD88-/- and STING-deficient macrophage experiments).

Orthotopic in vivo treatment demonstrates survival benefit and immune microenvironment remodeling in an immunocompetent setting, supporting translational plausibility beyond in vitro findings (Figures 8–9 descriptions; Discussion).
The study addresses a real clinical gap in meningioma systemic therapy and proposes a concrete, locally deliverable immunomodulatory approach (Abstract; Discussion).
key_concerns: Evidence remains preclinical/ex vivo; no clinical trial data are provided to establish safety, dosing, or efficacy of 8803 in patients with meningioma (Discussion).

The work spans many endpoints and high-dimensional analyses; while FDR is used in several places, multiplicity handling is not uniformly explicit across all non-omics readouts in the normalized text (Methods/Results).

Data/code availability is not concretely described in this normalized manuscript (e.g., explicit accession numbers/links for newly generated multiome data and analysis code), which can limit independent reanalysis (Methods/Additional Sections).

Some mechanistic claims (e.g., relative contributions of specific inflammatory death pathways) depend on integrating multiple assays; clearer prioritization of primary mechanistic endpoints would strengthen interpretability (Results/Discussion).
chief_reviewer.rationale: The paper presents a strong, well-supported preclinical case for STING agonism in meningiomas with both direct cytotoxic and immune-stromal remodeling mechanisms; the remaining gaps are chiefly translational (human dosing/safety) and transparency details, consistent with Tier 2 acceptance after minor revisions.
